name: pal_empty
journey: The head shrine of Inari, the kami of rice and good fortune. Around 10,000 vermilion torii gates climb Mount Inari in long tunnels.
Foxes (kitsune) are Inari's messengers, so fox statues guard the shrine, often with a key or a jewel in their mouths.
Home! Every journey of mine starts here~
Japan's first permanent capital, from 710. Over a thousand wild sika deer roam Nara Park, and Tōdai-ji houses a bronze Great Buddha about 15 m tall.
The deer are seen as messengers of the gods, and many bow back if you bow to them.
They bow if you bow! Very polite... until you have crackers.
